_comment: The single source of truth for how a clip becomes frames.
Read by BOTH sides on purpose. The backend samples frames in
the eval harness samples them from fixture files. If those two ever
differ, every number the harness prints is measured on input the
They already had differed: the harness carried a `thumbnail,` filter
the API does not use. `thumbnail` picks the most 'representative'
frames in a window rather than evenly-spaced ones, so the harness was
grading the model on a nicer sample than production sends — an
optimistic bias, invisible, and precisely the kind of thing an
A test on each side asserts against this file, so changing one
without the other fails CI rather than silently skewing results.
_videoFilterWhy: fps=1/1  — one frame per second, evenly spaced. A clip is usually one
activity for its whole length, so even sampling beats
clever selection and is far easier to reason about.
224x224  — a privacy control before it is a model detail: at that size
a face is about a dozen pixels across, so what leaves the
app cluster reads as 'a person on a court', not as a
recognisable child. The model wanting exactly this size is
crop     — after scaling up to cover, so nothing is letterboxed with
black bars the model would score as part of the image.
_extraArgsWhy: -an            — no audio reaches the output. A still cannot carry
sound, so this is about intent: a later edit to this
command cannot quietly start exporting any.
-map_metadata -1 — strip everything. A clip container can carry
creation time, device model, and GPS. CLAUDE.md's
'no location tracking' is a product rule, and this is
the point where a file could otherwise smuggle a
location out of the app cluster entirely.
